subject.title: Agent declared tools != effective session tools: no strict inheritance mode, no visibility, no clipping reason trace

question: Should OpenClaw add diagnostics-only declared/effective tool visibility first, or also add a default-off strict inheritance mode that fails sessions when declared and effective tools diverge?
rationale: The requested strict mode changes the authority boundary between agent config and lower runtime/session security layers, and likely adds config and protocol surface in a sensitive tool-permission area.

options.title: Diagnostics First
options.body: Expose declared, effective, and removed tools with structured reasons while keeping sandbox, subagent, ACP, provider, approval, and runtime-host clipping authoritative.

options.title: Default-Off Strict Parity
options.body: Add a strict inheritance option that fails closed when declared and effective tools diverge, with explicit override-layer reporting and upgrade tests.

options.title: Document Existing Clipping
options.body: Keep current runtime clipping behavior and document that declared agent tool config is not final session authority.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics First
recommendation.body: Expose declared, effective, and removed tools with structured reasons while keeping sandbox, subagent, ACP, provider, approval, and runtime-host clipping authoritative.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses the scoped capability profile, runtime tool policy, and gateway visibility surfaces where current history shows the clearest foundation work.
